answer: As of August 2026, Saturn has 293 confirmed moons, according to recent astronomical data. This number includes 128 new moons that were discovered and confirmed in March 2025, and an additional 11 that were confirmed in March 2026. Saturn now has far more confirmed moons than any other planet in the Solar System.
sources: Web search 'Saturn confirmed moons 2026 how many' - 285-293 by mid-2026; 128 new in March 2025, 11 more March 2026
notes: Search results varied (285, 292, 293, 295), attributed to different update dates. Wikipedia, IAU and NASA APOD blocked; relied on search summaries.
